title: 2026 U.S. House Election in New Jersey's 1st Congressional District
description: New Jersey's 1st Congressional District, covering Camden County and parts of Burlington and Gloucester Counties in South Jersey, is a heavily Democratic district where incumbent Rep. Donald Norcross (D) is seeking re-election against Republican Damon Galdo in the November 3, 2026 general election. The district leans strongly Democratic (44% registered Democrats vs. 19% Republicans), and nonpartisan forecasters rate the race as safe or solid Democratic. Norcross, a former electrician and union leader first elected in 2014, faces a general-election challenge from Galdo, a construction superintendent and conservative podcast host who ran unsuccessfully in the Republican primaries in 2022 and 2024 before securing the nomination unopposed in 2026.
polling_note: No public opinion polls specific to the NJ-01 general election were found. Nonpartisan election forecasters (Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, Sabato's Crystal Ball) all rate the race as Solid/Safe Democratic.

candidates.name: Donald Norcross
candidates.summary: Donald Norcross is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 1st Congressional District, first elected in November 2014. Born and raised in South Jersey, he began his career as an IBEW electrical apprentice in 1979 and rose through the labor ranks to become a business agent and president of the Southern New Jersey AFL-CIO Central Labor Council. In Congress, he has focused on labor rights, workforce development, affordable healthcare, and economic opportunity for working families.

candidates.name: Damon Galdo
candidates.summary: Damon Galdo is the Republican nominee for U.S. House in New Jersey's 1st Congressional District. A construction superintendent and carpenter by trade, he also hosts the conservative podcast 'Jersey Sure' and operates Americas Pulse Network. This is his third campaign for this congressional seat; he ran unsuccessfully in the Republican primaries in 2022 and 2024 before securing the 2026 Republican nomination unopposed.
